# Add import list tags to artists already in the library

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. Builds on [`feat/import-list-clean-library`](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/feat/import-list-clean-library). Reviewed in [#47](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/pull/47).

- New import list option, Tag Existing, with Sonarr's three modes. Don't Change, the default, tags only the artists the list adds. Add Only also adds the list's tags to artists already in the library, including the artist of a listed album that exists. Add and Remove does the same, and also takes a list's tag off an artist that's on no list with that tag any more, a tag added by hand included, as the warning under the option says. It acts only on lists with Enable Automatic Add, the ones a sync fetches; its help text says so.
- Add and Remove keeps a tag on an artist that any list with the tag names, a list with Enable Automatic Add off included, as Clean Library counts them all. It keeps the tag everywhere while any list with it that a sync fetches has failed, has never synced, or has failed since its last sync, as Clean Library does, and while one of those lists has an item tied to no artist by ID or by an album in the library, since matching by name alone could miss its artist, and while one of those lists' last fetch came back empty, which is more often a provider hiccup than an emptied list. An emptied list's tag then has to be removed by hand. An artist counts as listed by Clean Library's rules (its ID or a former one, its name, or a listed album), which both now take from one place, `ListedArtists`. Each artist is read again just before its tags are written, since the library list is cached, so a tag added meanwhile stays, and one deleted meanwhile is skipped. Albums listed by a former ID are found by a query per 500 IDs (`IAlbumService.FindByOldForeignIds`, its `LIKE` escaped) instead of loading every album, which a list with albums not in the library made happen on each sync.
- Tags are gathered across all lists and written once at the end of the sync, only for artists that lack them. An artist deleted during the sync, or a listed album whose artist row is gone, is skipped; before, one of them stopped the sync, so nothing was added or tagged that run. Only the tags column is written (`IArtistService.UpdateTags`, one batched `SetFields`, with a default body for services built against develop).
- A new artist on two lists, or the artist of a new album on two lists, gets both lists' tags, and so does an existing artist. The fetch now keeps an item per list: develop, like Sonarr, merged an item two lists share into one, so only one list, picked by timing, added its tags, or monitored an artist or album already in the library. A new artist still takes its monitoring and root folder from the first list that names it. An item the lists share is still searched for once; the other lists' copies take its result. Each new artist gets its own copy of a list's tags, so one list's tags never reach another list's artists.
- The option is in the list's edit modal and in bulk edit. A save that leaves it out, in bulk or for one list, keeps the stored mode. Migration 910 adds `ImportLists.TagExisting`, and 914 turns it into the mode, as Sonarr's 236 does, so a list that tagged existing artists becomes Add Only.

Tests: an existing artist tagged, nothing written with the option off or when the artist has the tags, the artist of an existing album tagged, a new artist on two lists, a new album on two lists (new and existing artist), the tags-only write against the database, a sync that still adds and tags when a listed artist is deleted mid-sync or a listed album has lost its artist (real services over the test database), the migration default, both modes that tag existing artists, Add Only never removing a tag, Add and Remove taking a tag off an artist on no list with it and keeping it for one on another list with the tag, for one listed by a former ID or through a listed album, while a list with the tag hasn't synced (never, disabled, or failed since), while an item isn't matched to an artist, while a list with the tag has no items, a tag added and an artist deleted after the library was read, an artist two lists share getting both lists' tags through the real fetch, a list with automatic add off keeping its tag on its artists without holding it, one search for an artist or album two lists share, the stored mode kept by a save that leaves it out, the removal against the database, migration 914 on SQLite and Postgres, each mode saved and read back through the list repository on both, and the former-ID album query (found, and `%` or `_` in an ID taken literally) on both. Each rule was broken on purpose and caught by a test, except migration 914's SQLite step: SQLite already stores the yes/no as 0 or 1, so that test passes without it. The Postgres step is the one that converts: without it, saving any mode fails there.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Configure import lists to tag artists already in your library, including artists matched through listed albums.
  * Choose to leave existing artists unchanged, add tags without removing them, or synchronize tags by adding and removing them.
  * Tags from multiple lists are combined, and tags not managed by those lists are preserved.
  * In synchronization mode, tags are removed only when relevant lists sync successfully and their artists can be matched; incomplete, empty or unresolved list data prevents removal.
  * Newly added artists also receive tags from their import lists.
